title: The vow
hook: a promise said out loud in front of people; Shantideva takes the vow, and the poem comes full circle
tomorrow: the vow is made. what keeps it from slipping?

segments.voice: Yesterday: the blind man's jewel. The awakening mind arose by chance, like a jewel in the heap. And the week behind it: I leave it all, said out loud, glad for all, may I be the medicine, and a bridge, a boat, a lamp.
screen: `A JEWEL IN THE HEAP.` → `I LEAVE IT ALL · SAID OUT LOUD.` → `GLAD FOR ALL · MEDICINE · A BRIDGE.`

segments.voice: There's a reason people make big promises in front of other people. Graduation pledges. Wedding vows. A new citizen with one hand raised. You could promise the same thing alone in your room, but it isn't quite the same. Said out loud, in front of witnesses, a promise starts to hold you. So, yesterday's question: jewel in hand, what does Shantideva promise next? He makes the vow, and he makes it in front of everyone.
screen: `ONE HAND RAISED.` → `SAID IN FRONT OF WITNESSES.` → `WHAT DOES HE PROMISE?`

segments.voice: Chapter three's heart is the bodhisattva vow. Shantideva says: just as the Buddhas of the past took up the awakening mind and trained in it step by step, so I too, for the good of the world, take it up and will train in it step by step. He isn't inventing a promise. He's stepping into one others have made. Then the line that closes the circle from two weeks ago. Remember hard to find, the blind turtle and this rare human life? Now he says: today my life is fruitful. This human life was well gained. Today I'm born into the Buddha's family. And at the chapter's end, in front of all the protectors, he invites the whole world to awakening, and until then, to happiness. The witnesses matter. So does the word today. Not someday, after more practice. The rare life from the first week gets its point in this one. Today my life is fruitful.
screen: `AS THE BUDDHAS BEFORE ME DID.` · `STEP BY STEP.` · `HARD TO FIND, NOW FRUITFUL.` · `IN FRONT OF ALL THE PROTECTORS.` · then, large: `TODAY MY LIFE IS FRUITFUL.`

segments.voice: Sit up, hands resting together. Think of one person or group whose good you care about, and find one promise for them you can actually keep, small and specific. Say it out loud, quietly, once, as if someone you respect were listening. Then sit with it.
The vow: Shantideva taking up the awakening mind for the good of the world, as the Buddhas before him did, in front of witnesses.
Your line: today my life is fruitful. Hard to find, and now put to use. Three chapters read; two weeks done.

howItsDone: In Mahayana Buddhism the bodhisattva vow is often taken in a ceremony before a teacher and images of the Buddhas, and some practitioners recite verses from this chapter daily to renew it.

fork.setup: you want to promise your little sister you'll help with her reading. what fits Shantideva's vow?
options: promise to help her every single day, forever, so it sounds big enough.
make a specific promise you can keep, say it to her, and start this week.
don't promise anything, in case life gets busy and you let her down.
fork.reveal: Shantideva's vow is said before witnesses and kept step by step. a real, specific promise, said out loud and begun, is the shape of it.
